title: Onprem airgapped GPU drivers & offline licensing deep dive

Agreed next steps: provide signed artifact bundle with checksums, offline license key flow, and schedule install window for proof-of-concept cluster. SE to run initial perf knobs and share expected latency/throughput for target model mix.

Offline licensing (GPU drivers and Redwood runtime)
KV cache persistence and warm-up strategies
Batching & quantization tradeoffs for latency vs cost
VPC/on-prem networking, KMS, and audit logging

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-02
Start time (UTC): 14:00
Duration: 62 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood), Mark Chen (Aurelius Infra), Leila Gomez (Aurelius Security), Tom Reynolds (Aurelius ML)

[00:00] Sofia: all right hi everyone thanks for joining. quick check audio/video?
[00:10] Mark: yup good here, thanks Sofia.
[00:15] Sofia: cool, um our goal for today is to go deep on the on-prem airgapped flow — artifact delivery, offline licensing for the gpu drivers and the runtime, and then some runtime tuning notes (kv cache, batching, quant). we'll try to leave 10 minutes at the end for next steps.
[00:30] Daniel: yeah i'll lead the artifact and driver compatibility piece. Priya will jump in on license and security details.
[00:40] Leila: thanks. to call out up front we need SOC2-like audit evidence for any offline license handoff and the artifact transfer must be via a controlled channel we approve.
[00:50] Priya: understood, we'll include checksums, PGP signatures, and an install checklist.
[01:05] Tom: also, for the perf side we run mixed workloads — some 8k seq chat inference and a few high qps embeddings endpoints. we'll share exact numbers but expecting peak ~600 qps across cluster.
[01:20] Daniel: good, that helps. quick question on the cluster: are you planning GPU passthrough VMs or k8s node pool?
[01:30] Mark: we'll be on k8s with GPU node pools (NVIDIA A100s, currently driver 520.xx installed by infra).
[01:40] Daniel: 520 series is fine, we usually recommend 525+ for the latest CUDA/cuDNN paths with our quantized kernels but 520 can work with a pinned runtime. we'll document exact compatibility.
[01:55] Sofia: should we walk through artifact contents? Daniel?
[02:00] Daniel: sure. the artifact bundle we're proposing contains: runtime tar (redwood-runtime-2.1.0.tar.gz), driver shim and helper scripts (driver-bundle.tar.gz), offline license blob (license.key.enc), install scripts, and a post-install validation harness. we'll ship a PGP-signed manifest and SHA256 sums.
[02:20] Mark: how big is the runtime tar? large images are tricky to transfer into the airgapped zone.
[02:30] Daniel: typically the full bundle is ~4.2GB for the runtime+drivers+docs. if you need smaller we can provide a minimal runtime (no precompiled kernels) and then an optional kernel pack. splitting into two artifacts is an option.
[02:50] Leila: on transfer — we require SFTP into our transfer VM, not public urls. can you support that?
[02:58] Priya: yes we can stage the bundle on a Redwood SFTP endpoint and provide creds over your approved channel; manifest will be signed.
[03:10] Tom: on the license, does the offline license require outbound calls for activation? we can't allow that in the airgapped environment.
[03:18] Priya: no, the offline flow is key-wrap based. we provide an encrypted license file that you install and a local validation binary that verifies signature against an offline public key. activation is offline — no call home. the only caveat is periodic revalidation if you opt for short lived entitlements.
[03:35] Leila: we'll need the revalidation window to be configurable and at least 180 days.
[03:40] Priya: configurable yes, default 90 days but can be extended to 365 or more for enterprise.
[03:48] Daniel: switching to drivers — we bundle a GPU driver shim which coordinates with your system driver (we don't overwrite distro drivers by default). the shim ensures the runtime sees the correct CUDA symbols and can load our quantized kernels. if you want full isolation we can ship a URM (userland runtime) that sits in the container.
[04:10] Mark: any kernel module changes required? infra is sensitive about host kernel changes.
[04:16] Daniel: no kernel module changes are required for the normal flow; everything is userland. only scenario that needs host-level modifications is if you want persistent device assignment via VFIO in a special setup, which you said you're not doing.
[04:30] Tom: let's talk perf knobs — kv cache warmup times are a big deal for us because we do lots of chat sessions and cold-starts kill p99 latency.
[04:40] Daniel: agreed. our runtime supports persistent kv cache across restarts; we offer two approaches: 1) disk-backed persistent cache with mmap'd storage (fast recovery but needs ephemeral space) or 2) a pre-warmed snapshot you load at container start. both are in the artifact bundle.
[04:58] Tom: do you store kv cache in a shared NFS? we prefer local NVMe.
[05:04] Daniel: local NVMe is ideal — lower tail latency. shared NFS works but adds variability. we'll include tooling to checkpoint the kv cache to local NVMe.
[05:15] Sofia: what's the expected warm-up time with a pre-warmed snapshot for a 16B decoder model?
[05:22] Daniel: for a 16B quantized model on A100 with our persistent cache it can warm in ~6-12 seconds to p50 and p95 recovers in ~30s depending on seq-length distribution. without pre-warm it's more like 2-3 minutes for stable tail behavior.
[05:40] Tom: that's better than I expected. what about batching — we need sub-100ms for short completion calls for a few routes.
[05:50] Daniel: there's a tradeoff. continuous small-batching mode keeps latency low at the cost of throughput. we can set per-route SLO policies: low-latency routes use batch size 1..4 and have a tight micro-timeout (e.g., 8-12ms) and background higher-throughput routes use larger batching. We'll include suggested configs based on your qps numbers.
[06:15] Mark: quantization — we run some sensitive clinical text; do you see accuracy regressions with 4-bit quant?
[06:24] Daniel: quantization affects some workloads. we support mixed precision profiles: FP16, int8 and 4-bit QK variants. our recommendation: start with FP16 or int8 QAT for sensitive clinical text and use 4-bit for high throughput non-sensitive inference (embeddings). we also provide eval harnesses in the bundle to run your prompt set and compare delta.
[06:45] Tom: can we run automatic A/B rollbacks if quality drops?
[06:50] Priya: yes— the rollout config includes automatic fallback to a pinned model variant if quality thresholds are breached, and you can disable auto-rollback if you prefer manual.
[06:58] Leila: audit trail — we need to see when licenses were installed and who performed the install.
[07:04] Daniel: the install script produces an audit log (signed) and we generate an install manifest that includes installer user, host fingerprint, timestamp, and artifact checksum; that file is signed by Redwood's PGP key.
[07:20] Sofia: quick detour — network segmentation and KMS. Leila you mentioned you want to use your HSM for key wrapping?
[07:27] Leila: yes, we need the license file to be encrypted under our KMS-wrapped key so only our environment can decrypt.
[07:33] Priya: we support providing a customer public key; we will encrypt the license blob under that key so decryption is only possible with your private key. we will also provide a sample script to integrate with your HSM to unwrap during install.
[07:45] Mark: any concern about driver signatures or kernel module signing with enterprise distributions?
[07:50] Daniel: since we avoid kernel modules, signing is only relevant for the runtime container images and the driver userland components; those are PGP-signed. if you require distro-level signing we can provide instructions to add our keys to your package manager trust store.
[08:05] Tom: let's talk benchmarking — what's the recommended baseline tests you run in a POC?
[08:12] Daniel: we run a mixed workload harness: 60% chat (avg seq 1.5k tokens), 30% embeddings, 10% long completion. measure p50/p95/p99 latency and cost per token. we also run KV cache stress test and a cold-start scenario. we'll include templates in the artifacts.
[08:30] Mark: can Redwood run these tests against our cluster or do we run them internally?
[08:35] Sofia: we prefer joint tests — Redwood SE runs the harness with your infra access in a controlled window; results are shared and we tune configs together.
[08:45] Leila: access model — we only allow temporary SSH jumpbox creds and scoped service accounts.
[08:50] Daniel: that's fine. our runbook supports jumpbox access patterns and we can ship a read-only telemetry exporter that you can choose to enable.
[09:02] Tom: telemetry — what telemetry does the runtime send back by default? we need PII controls.
[09:08] Priya: offline install sends zero telemetry by default. for hosted telemetry you must opt-in. any logs we provide can be filtered and scrubbed; we share a telemetry manifest in the bundle.
[09:20] Sofia: okay i want to circle back to action steps — Daniel, you will stage the artifact, Priya will give license details; Mark will confirm install window. anything else?
[09:30] Mark: just one more — driver version support matrix please, especially if we stay on 520 series.
[09:36] Daniel: yes we'll include a compatibility matrix (driver version -> CUDA -> recommended runtime flags).
[09:42] Tom: last q: offline license rotation — what's the manual process?
[09:48] Priya: you'll run our rotation tool which generates a new CSR, Redwood signs and returns a wrapped license, and you install it. rotation can be fully offline using your HSM. we'll provide step-by-step.
[10:00] Sofia: great. i'll restate next steps and owners.
[10:05] Sofia: Daniel to stage artifacts + checksums (due 12/06). Priya to send offline license docs and sample key (due 12/06). Mark to confirm install window and provide host list (due 12/04). Tom to provide model mix and expected qps (due 12/04).
[10:25] Mark: confirmed. thanks all.
[10:30] Sofia: we'll schedule the 2-hour install slot once we have the host list. thanks everyone, bye.

-- End of transcript --
